Hero of the Month - LCDR Radcliffe “Pete” Denniston Jr., USN

Lieutenant Commander Radcliffe “Pete” Denniston Jr. was born on February 5, 1916, in Wauwatosa, Wisconsin. A graduate of Lawrence College, he entered the Navy as an aviation cadet in 1936 and trained at Pensacola, Florida before joining Torpedo Squadron Five (VT-5) aboard the USS Yorktown (CV-5).

When the Pacific front of WWII opened, Denniston participated in strikes against the Gilbert and Marshall Islands, Salamaua, Lae, and Tulagi. His most distinguished actions came during the Battle of the Coral Sea in May 1942, where he successfully scored torpedo hits on two Japanese carriers while facing intense anti-aircraft fire and enemy fighter opposition. For his extraordinary heroism during the attacks at Tulagi Harbor and Coral Sea, he was awarded the Navy Cross.

Following the battle of Coral Sea, Denniston returned to Fort Lauderdale, Florida as an instructor and later became chief flight instructor. On September 25, 1943, he assumed command of Torpedo Squadron Eleven (VT-11).

During his second combat tour, he took part in missions against Okinawa, Formosa, Luzon, Leyte, and the Second Battle of the Philippine Sea. On November 13, 1944, while leading a glide-bombing attack against enemy shipping in Manila Harbor, his aircraft encountered heavy anti-aircraft fire. Denniston’s final transmission was: “Plane hit, am going in.” He was never seen again.

LCDR Denniston is buried at the ABMC Manila American Cemetery in the Philippines.

Nabulabog ang pagtulog ng mga residente ng Bgy. Pasong Putik, Quezon City dahil sa sumiklab na sunog sa residential area sa panulukan ng Bautista at Everlasting Streets, pasado 1 a.m. ngayong Miyerkules, Mayo 13.

Umabot sa ikatlong alarma ang sunog na idineklarang "fire out" ng BFP pasado alas-3 ng madaling araw. 

Inaalam pa ang sanhi ng sunog at bilang ng mga pamilyang naapektuhan. | via @punongmhistrado

data.english_translation: The sleep of the Bgy residents is disturbed by the fires in the residential area on the corner of the Baptist and Eversing Streets, past 1 a.m. this Wednesday, May 13. The fire reached a third alarm declared "fire out" of BFPym after six o’clock in the morning. Mother knows the cause of the fire and the number of families affected.
